name: Saints Fabian and Sebastian
dates: Third and early fourth centuries · Rome
history: Two Roman martyrs kept on the same day. Fabian, a layman, was chosen as pope in 236 and governed the Church for fourteen years before dying in the persecution of Decius. Sebastian, tradition holds, was a soldier who encouraged Christians in prison and was shot with arrows for his faith. He survived, was nursed back to health, confronted the emperor and was clubbed to death.
life: Eusebius tells that when the clergy and people of Rome met to choose a bishop in 236, a dove settled on the head of Fabian, a layman who had come in from the country, and he was acclaimed at once. He organised the city’s deacons and districts, cared for the cemeteries of the martyrs, and is said to have sent missionaries to Gaul. Arrested when Decius ordered every citizen to sacrifice to the gods, he died in January 250, one of the first victims; his tomb, with its Greek inscription, survives in the catacomb of Callixtus. Of Sebastian we know for certain only that he was a martyr buried on the Appian Way, where a basilica bears his name. His later story tells of an officer of the imperial guard who was tied to a stake and pierced with arrows, then cared for by a widow named Irene. In times of plague Christians turned to him, and painters of every age have shown him.
prayerTo: Saints Fabian and Sebastian, you held fast to Christ under the sword and the arrow. Pray for the Pope and for all who govern the Church, that they may be faithful shepherds. Pray for soldiers and for the sick, and for me, that I may be brave in small things and faithful in great ones. Amen.
penance: Pray today for the Pope and for Christians serving in the armed forces. Offer a small act of endurance, such as standing for your prayers, for those who suffer for their faith.
meditation: Fabian did not seek to lead; he was called, and he served. Sebastian was struck down and got up again. Where is God asking you to get up again?
prayer: Be mindful of our weakness, almighty God, and because the burden of our sins weighs heavily upon us, may the glorious intercession of blessed N., Your Martyr and Bishop, sustain us. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
